entropy: Exactly two fresh key productions in Phase A, one per scheme, each exactly one 32-byte read from /dev/urandom inside the isolated helper process. Invalid scalar stops with failure; there is no entropy or key-generation retry. Secret scalars never leave helper memory, are never stored or printed, and carry no memory-erasure theorem. Ephemeral test keys are not future live T1 catalogue keys and cannot be reused after the process ends; production custody remains a future fresh scope. The existing Ed25519 wallet is never read.

phases.A_PRODUCE: Source, materialization, toolchain and dependency pins are fully frozen before the first native command. At most one offline Rust helper build, then exactly two helper calls. Stop at COMPLETED_AWAITING_FRESH_ACTUAL_PUBLIC_INPUT_AUDIT; build_inputs.py then generates the public VI inputs as an ordinary data-only step.
phases.B_EVALUATE: Only after a fresh audit of the actual produced public inputs and a new exact eight-case AUTH: eight sequential VI evaluations, zero retries. Old keygen/K6/K10 authorities are spent and never reused; no C2/K8/K9/K10 rerun occurs.

pins.k256EcdsaSourcePacket: k256 0.13.4 + ecdsa 0.16.9, 12 source files plus 4 licenses in the indexed primary crate packet

signingRoutes.chosen: High-level k256 Signer::try_sign on the exact Core signing_message bytes for both schemes. Core verify_intent uses the matching Verifier::verify(message), and VI supplies sha2_256(message) to the Cardano builtin, so one signature serves both consumers.
signingRoutes.rejectedDoubleHash: Passing the 32-byte digest to Signer would apply a second outer SHA-256 and fail Core verification.
signingRoutes.rejectedPrehashOnMessage: Passing the full message to sign_prehash/sign_raw would skip the outer SHA-256 Core applies. The prehash route on the digest is byte-equivalent for both schemes (Schnorr zero auxiliary bytes; ECDSA deterministic RFC6979) and is documented, not used, so no auxiliary randomness is guessed.
